text:
eli: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a 'fastpath' escape from the continuous batcher. If requests bypass coalescing, how do we account for cost and fairness?
maya: +1. We need a clear tag so billing/telemetry can split coalesced vs fastpath units. Otherwise chargeback will be wrong.
sam: Proposal: add `path` enum on request: `coalesce|fastpath|spill`. Emit metric `batch.request_path{path}` and weight cost accordingly.
nora: Important: fastpath increases CPU pressure. We should prefer tenant throttles over unbounded fastpath. Otherwise we trade latency for noisy neighbors.
eli: Also need a graceful-eviction handshake: if the batcher decides to evict, it should attach `evict_reason` and `queue_age_ms` so downstream can decide to fastpath or retry.
anton: For billing rollouts, consider a soft window: measure delta for 1 week then apply chargeback. Customers hate surprise billing.
maya: Observability checklist: per-tenant counters: `enqueued_total`, `released_to_fastpath_total`, `evicted_total`, `queued_age_histogram`. Dashboards + an alert for sustained `released_to_fastpath / enqueued > 0.005`.
sam: Example admission config sketch for canary:
```
admission:
  max_queue_ms: 120
  fastpath_threshold: 6   # if batch size < this, prefer fastpath
  evict_burst_limit: 50
  tenant_throttle_pct: 5
```
nora: Add trace tags too: `batch_id`, `queue_age_ms`, `path`, `evict_reason` so we can follow one request from enqueue -> serve.
dev-bot: deploy scheduled to canary cluster: Tue 03:00 UTC (will post results).
eli: safety note — add `cost_override: deny_fastpath` flag so free-tier or promo customers cannot trigger fastpath during experiments.
maya: I'll draft the RFC follow-up PR with metrics, config defaults, and rollout plan (canary -> gradual). Link to current RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfc/continuous-batcher-ops-1234
sam: heads-up: ML infra reported ~12% CPU bump during earlier fastpath microtest; we need headroom gating.
nora: TL;DR: fastpath is OK if we: 1) tag requests, 2) emit metrics+traces, 3) add tenant throttles, 4) canary the rollout, 5) have a chargeback/soft-window. :thumbsup:
